thread:
allan: Quick RFC follow-up — I sketched a signal flow for soft-lease eviction that tries to avoid global spikes when tenants are evicted. posting the sequence and tradeoffs we discussed in the call earlier.

allan: TL;DR: introduce an eviction signal that is local to the admission layer, decoupled from token accounting. Admission emits `EVICT_WARN` -> tenant gets soft-shed window -> if unhealed, `EVICT_COMMIT` which triggers graceful handback to backup pool.

rachel: Love the decoupling idea. main question: how do we ensure fairness scheduler doesn't overreact to transient probe spikes?

devin: Proposal: add a sliding suppression window on the scheduler where an eviction warning only reduces weight by X% immediately, and then ramps down further if errors persist. avoids full throttle for noisy spikes.

kevin: important implementation detail — we need an explicit interface between admission and quota-shard: `EvictionSignal { tenant_id, stage, reason, expires_at }`. simple HTTP/GRPC push from admission to quota-shard.

allan: agree. keep payload tiny. reason enumerated to avoid free-text. stage in {WARN, PROBATION, COMMIT}. expires_at allows automatic healing.

sasha: how about abuse prevention? If a tenant intentionally tries to keep generating WARN signals (probing) to game fallback pools, we should add an abuse_score bump on repeated WARNs from same tenant in short window.

devin: yep — abuse_score should be updated by quota-shard when it observes repeated WARN->COMMIT cycles. And it should affect routing priority (lower).

allan: tradeoffs: stronger abuse penalties help shared pools but risk punishing bursty legitimate tenants. We should expose a policy flag per org: `eviction_aggressiveness: {conservative, default, aggressive}` so enterprise customers can opt in.

kevin: operational hooks needed: metrics and traces for every signal, and a per-tenant timeline API. minimal metrics: `eviction_warn_count`, `eviction_commit_count`, `eviction_recover_count`, `eviction_latency_ms`.

mike: +1. Also need a canary rollout for the eviction handler. start with a small percent of heavy tenants and monitor tail latency + error rate.

allan: rough sketch of pseudocode for admission -> quota-shard flow:
```
# admission (incoming request)
if tenant.over_quota():
  emit EvictionSignal(tenant, stage=\"WARN\", reason=\"quota_burst\", expires_at=now+30s)
  respond 429 (soft) with header X-Eviction-Warn
else:
  allow()
```

# quota-shard:
```
on EvictionSignal(s):
  if s.stage == \"WARN\":
    tenant.weight *= (1 - heuristic(\"warn_immediate_drop\"))
    schedule check at s.expires_at
  if repeated_warns > N: abuse_score += 1
  if s.stage == \"COMMIT\": move_to_backup_pool(tenant)
```

rachel: two interface questions: 1) should admission push signals or quota-shard pull tenant metrics? 2) how do we coordinate cross-region evictions?

sasha: 1) push is simpler for low latency. pull becomes eventual and more complex. we can keep push as primary and have a periodic reconcile (pull) to fix drift.

kevin: 2) cross-region: emit region-scoped signals with a global coordinator that can escalate to global COMMIT if multiple regions report PROBATION concurrently. but aim to keep most logic local to avoid cascading failures.

allan: long-term refactor note: we should migrate eviction policy logic out of admission and into a policy-service that both admission and quota-shard consult. that will make rollout and experimentation easier (feature flags + weights per org).

mike: ops-bot: deploy plan? :robot_face:

ops-bot: @channel Starting staged rollout plan: 5% tenants (non-prod) -> monitor 72h -> 25% -> monitor 24h -> global. Alerting: page on eviction_commit_rate > baseline * 3 for 5m.

allan: next steps: I'll open RFC PR with diagrams and message schema. assign implementers: @rachel on admission changes, @kevin on quota-shard + metrics, @devin on scheduler tuning, @sasha on abuse-scoring heuristics.

rachel: tiny nit — please include example HTTP schema for EvictionSignal in RFC.

allan: will do. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
